help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The measures planned by the government were presented yesterday.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The problem that has existed for years is still not solved.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Everything that belongs to the participle sits between the article and the participle; the noun comes last.
help.tips[0].en.text: das | von mir | gelesene | Buch · die | gestern | geschriebene | E-Mail · die | in der Fabrik | hergestellten | Produkte · der | ständig | zunehmende | Verkehr. Everything between the article and the participle belongs to the participle.
help.tips[0].en.title: Article … complements … participle + ending … noun
help.tips[0].en.trap: 'the by the government planned measures' is impossible in English, so the eye stalls at 'die von'. Train it: article, then jump to the noun, then read the middle.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: the constantly increasing traffic = the traffic that is constantly increasing
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: A Partizip II attribute unfolds into a passive: the heating was repaired yesterday.
help.tips[1].en.text: Partizip II → passive or Perfekt: die hergestellten Produkte = die Produkte, die hergestellt werden / wurden. das gelesene Buch = das Buch, das gelesen wurde / das ich gelesen habe. Partizip I → active present: der zunehmende Verkehr = der Verkehr, der zunimmt.
help.tips[1].en.title: Unfold into a relative clause
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: the figures named in the report
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: the palace that was built in the 18th century → the palace built in the 18th century
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: Passive and finished → Partizip II gebaut; after das in the nominative neuter the ending is -e.
help.tips[2].en.text: das Team, das gut organisiert ist → das gut organisierte Team · die Brücke, die 2020 eröffnet wurde → die 2020 eröffnete Brücke · das Unternehmen, das schnell wächst → das schnell wachsende Unternehmen. Move the complements in front, turn the verb into a participle, add the ending.
help.tips[2].en.title: Fold a relative clause into an attribute
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: the running engine — a running engine — with the engine running
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: all the colleagues involved in the project — with sharply rising temperatures
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: The participle takes adjective endings: after ein in the nominative masculine, -er.
help.tips[3].en.text: die hergestellten Produkte (-en, plural after die), das gelesene Buch (-e), der gemachte Plan (-e), ein gemachter Plan (-er). Same table as any adjective.
help.tips[3].en.title: The ending comes from the article, not the participle
help.context.en: The bridge planned by the city and opened in 2020 has noticeably reduced the traffic in the centre that had been increasing for years. The figures named in the report confirm the decision taken at the time. The well-organised team responsible for the project is now working on the second phase, which begins in spring.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: Complements go between article and participle.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: The participle takes an adjective ending.
help.hookEn: Unpack and build the long noun phrases of newspapers and reports, like die von der Stadt geplante Brücke.
help.introEn: The extended participial attribute is the signature of written German: a participle with its own complements, all packed between the article and the noun. Das von mir gelesene Buch (the book read by me), die gestern geschriebene E-Mail, der schnell gemachte Plan, die in der Fabrik hergestellten Produkte, das seit Jahren bestehende Problem, der ständig zunehmende Verkehr. Every one unfolds into a relative clause — das Buch, das ich gelesen habe; der Verkehr, der ständig zunimmt — and folding a relative clause into a participial attribute is the reverse operation. Reading strategy: when you meet an article followed by something that is not the noun, jump to the noun, then read backwards. Writing strategy: use it once or twice in a formal text for compactness; more than that and the sentence collapses. Partizip II for passive / completed (hergestellt, geschrieben), Partizip I for active / ongoing (zunehmend, bestehend, laufend), and adjective endings on the participle as always. In this quiz you supply the participle with its ending inside long attributes, in all four cases, with and without an article — you decide Partizip I or II from the meaning. Folding and unfolding whole relative clauses is drilled earlier in the course.
help.rememberEn[0]: Article → (jump to) noun → read the middle backwards.
help.rememberEn[1]: Partizip II = passive/done; Partizip I = active/ongoing; both take adjective endings.
help.recallEn.known: From "Partizip als Adjektiv": der um acht ankommende Zug.
help.recallEn.today: Longer attributes with several complements, read from the article to the noun.
sentences[0].whyEn: A passive result: Partizip II + ending — beschlossenen.
sentences[1].whyEn: It still exists (active, ongoing): Partizip I — bestehende.
sentences[2].whyEn: It is increasing now: zunehmend + dative -en — zunehmenden.
sentences[5].whyEn: It is growing (active): wachsend + -es after ein — wachsendes.
sentences[9].whyEn: They are rising (active): steigend + dative plural -en.
sentences[10].whyEn: It was built: erbaute — er- without ge-.
